integrity: The proof is an exact hyperboloid-model reduction. Supporting hyperplanes are encoded by their Lorentz pairings with the simplex vertices; the regular-simplex Gram inverse converts unit-normal normalization into a strictly convex quadratic optimization on coordinate faces of a cube. The discrete optimum is uniquely attained at k=ceil(d/2), and equality conditions give all minimizing supports. A standalone symbolic checker replays the critical identities and the tetrahedral specialization.
scientific_limitations: The formula is for Lassak's support-hyperplane width, not for other inequivalent hyperbolic notions of width such as equidistant thickness. It covers compact regular simplices of finite positive edge length and does not classify nonregular or ideal simplices. A differently phrased or poorly indexed prior observation remains a residual originality risk.
title: Exact Lassak thickness of every regular hyperbolic simplex
